title: BUILD-005-service-health-monitor
universal_lens: The transition from open-source leverage to production deployment is modeled as a constrained optimization over a Hilbert space of system states. The operator projects unbounded external repositories onto a bounded, secure subspace defined by explicit legal and security boundary conditions, ensuring structural integrity.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this maps to a conformal prediction framework where the sandbox acts as a calibration set. We infer the reliability distribution of external OSS components before updating the posterior probability of their safe integration into the core Galaxy Sports Intelligence engine.
gse_mapping: GSE situational reasoning treats the build card as a discrete state-transition matrix. The system enforces a strict progression from documentation/sandbox states to application code states only upon satisfying an explicit approval predicate, preventing unauthorized mutations in the operational manifold.

primitives.name: Open-Source Leverage Projection Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Why It Matters This improves decision quality, revenue, speed, support, retention, trust, or cost savings by converting open-source leverage into a bounded GSE workflow.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: L: Open-source leverage (dimensionless), W: Bounded GSE workflow (state vector), V: Value metric (currency/time)
primitives.assumptions: The projection operator is linear and preserves the intrinsic utility of the open-source component while strictly enforcing boundary constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the dimensionality of the external OSS exceeds the capacity of the bounded GSE workflow, leading to integration singularities.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to projecting high-dimensional market data into a low-dimensional alpha factor space within GSI, retaining signal while discarding noise.
layer2.telemetry: Reduction in manual coordination hours and measurable SaaS cost avoidance.

primitives.name: Security Boundary Constraint Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Security Boundary No secrets, production data, customer PII, proprietary method docs, payment data, or production source keys.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S: Secrets/PII (boolean flag), D: Production Data (dataset), C: Compliance threshold (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: The constraint kernel acts as a hard filter; any state vector containing non-zero elements of S or D is immediately rejected.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the definition of 'production data' becomes ambiguous during dynamic runtime environment shifts.

layer2.mapping: Functions identically to a risk-parity constraint in quantitative portfolio construction, zeroing out exposure to forbidden asset classes.
layer2.telemetry: Zero incidence of secret leakage or PII exposure in sandbox environments.

primitives.name: Documentation-First State Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Start in docs or a sandbox and only move into app code after explicit approval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t: Time step (discrete), A: Approval predicate (boolean), \Delta: State transition operator
primitives.assumptions: State transitions are strictly sequential and require an external boolean trigger (A) to proceed from the documentation subspace to the execution subspace.
primitives.breakdown_regime: System halts if the approval predicate remains undefined indefinitely, creating a deadlock in the development pipeline.

layer2.mapping: Mirrors the pre-trade compliance checks in algorithmic trading, where order books cannot be accessed until risk limits are formally validated.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of build cards successfully transitioning from docs to app code without triggering rollback protocols.
